nodes.name: Hourly Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — every 6 h. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Route by Work Type
nodes.notes: Routes each item to one of 3 lanes: sync, async + fallback. Watch out: Unmatched items go to the fallback output; without one they are silently dropped.

nodes.name: Process 'sync' → MySQL
nodes.notes: Inserts a row into the MySQL table using fields auto-mapped from the incoming item. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: MySQL connection. Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.

nodes.name: Fast-Track 'async' + Alert
nodes.notes: Sends a Telegram message to the configured chat — the same bot can also receive replies, so this doubles as a two-way ops channel. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Telegram bot token. Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.

nodes.name: Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
nodes.notes: Inserts a row into the MySQL table using fields auto-mapped from the incoming item. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: MySQL connection. Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.

nodes.name: Merge Routed Work
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Align Field Names
nodes.notes: Normalizes field names so every source feeds the same downstream schema.

# Automate a multi-step process: MySQL

**Pattern:** Workflow Automation · **Level:** Beginner · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers summarization work end to end across MySQL and Telegram.

It moves through 7 working steps, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Route by Work Type
3. Process 'sync' → MySQL
4. Fast-Track 'async' + Alert
5. Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
6. Merge Routed Work
7. Align Field Names

## Why it exists

Doing summarization work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Route by Work Type → Process 'sync' → MySQL → Fast-Track 'async' + Alert → Hold Unknown Types (DLQ) → Merge Routed Work → Align Field Names

## Use it for

- Teams keeping MySQL and Telegram aligned by hand for summarization
- Summarization work where "Route by Work Type" is still a manual step before MySQL
- Summarization work that only reaches MySQL on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps MySQL and Telegram in step for summarization, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed MySQL or Telegram call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 7 nodes in this summarization build
- Branches rejoin before MySQL, so a summarization run reports once rather than 7 times
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 7 nodes for summarization before wiring MySQL
- 7 nodes, each with a doc card explaining what it does for summarization

## Before first run
Connect credentials: MySQL connection; Telegram bot token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Unrecognized work types are parked in a dead-letter lane instead of erroring the whole run or silently dropping the item — new event kinds will show up eventually, and this is where you'd notice one without losing it. One kind is deliberately routed through a sub-workflow to show how heavier per-type logic can be extracted without touching this router at all.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Send a work-type value that matches no switch rule and confirm it lands in the dead-letter branch.
2. Add a new work type and its own handling branch.
3. Replace the direct-write branch with a sub-workflow call, matching the pattern already used for the first kind.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**MySQL connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.
_Gotcha:_ Remote access often needs the n8n server's IP allow-listed.

**Telegram bot token**
Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Get your chat ID by messaging the bot then opening api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your summarization process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- MySQL: grant the user only the tables this workflow touches; avoid `GRANT ALL` on the schema.
- Telegram: the bot token is a bearer credential — rotate it if it ever appears in an execution log.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole summarization payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
